reported.title: pH conversion omits division by 500 mV/pH
reported.description: computePh() at line 23 simply returns the millivolt value unchanged instead of dividing by the 500 mV/pH scale, so the printed value is the raw millivolt reading. Measured output of 2966.76 pH against an injected 5.5-6.0 pH (and 5000 pH at 4.01 s) confirms the missing /500 scaling. Firmware printed 5000 pH at 4.01 s while the injected input was 10.0 to 10.0 pH: off by 4990.0 pH (tolerance ±0.2). 7 of 7 values were wrong.

reported.title: Alert LED driven from unscaled millivolt value
reported.description: The threshold test at line 66 compares lastPh, which is actually millivolts (see line 23), against ALERT_PH = 7.20, so the LED is essentially always HIGH since any real probe reading exceeds 7.2 mV. Measured D13 wrong for 4850 ms and 2530 ms in the ramp/glitch scenarios shows the alert state does not follow the injected pH. D13 was in the wrong state for 4850 ms across 6 interval(s), first at 500 ms: D13 was not HIGH for 500 ms while required (grace 500 ms).

judge_input.spec:
- Linearized pH probe on A0 with scale 500 mV/pH (0 mV → pH 0.0); low-pH alert LED on D13.
- Convert ADC samples using a 5.000 V / 1023 full-scale span, then divide millivolts by 500 to obtain pH.
- Print exactly one line every 1000 ms matching `pH: <value>` with two decimal places.
- Printed pH must stay within ±0.20 of the injected probe value.
- Drive D13 HIGH when reported pH is below 7.20; otherwise drive D13 LOW.
- Keep logging while the alert LED is on or off.
